minutes.headline: Commission backed a new one-page intent form to speed review of minor work, with shorter guidelines; no formal vote on it.
minutes.summary: The commission approved two sets of earlier minutes, then spent most of the meeting on the chair's proposal for a one-page form that sorts minor work from work needing a certificate to alter, submitted electronically and possibly without a fee. Members discussed how to answer quickly without breaching open meeting law and agreed the chair would ask town counsel. Other items were recruiting a fifth member, the deteriorating 50 Main Street church, the master plan meeting, and a historical commission survey grant.

votes.motion: Approve the minutes of 12 December and 8 August, subject to one more review for typos.

budget_items.what_was_said: The chair noted the bylaw requires no fees but the guidelines list an initial application fee and a higher review fee, and asked whether they can be waived. Members said fees seem counterproductive.
The historical commission is applying for a matching grant to hire a consultant to survey historic houses; the town approved half the matching money.

decisions.decision: Nathan will talk to the owners of 50 Main Street and ask them to come to a commission meeting.
The chair will email a young resident active in the master plan and green communities committees to ask if she will join.
The chair will ask town counsel how to streamline approvals within open meeting law.
Members were comfortable proceeding with the new form; the chair will circulate the forms and seek an editable Word file of the guidelines.

The chair will ask town counsel how the commission can answer applicants quickly without breaching open meeting law.
Members questioned the application and review fees listed in the guidelines, which the bylaw does not require, and said fees seem counterproductive.
A member will ask the owners of 50 Main Street, the deteriorating old Methodist church, to come to a commission meeting.
The chair will email a young resident active in the master plan and green communities committees to ask her to fill the open fifth seat.

why_it_matters: A homeowner planning minor exterior work in the district could face a shorter, electronic, possibly fee-free review, but the fee and approval process depend on counsel's advice and the commission's next steps.
The commission is acting on a deteriorating historic church only by asking the owners to attend a meeting, so the building's condition is not yet being addressed through any formal step.
